headline: Discussed barriers to reviewing opioid overdose deaths; no case reviews have started yet
summary: The workgroup discussed why local opioid fatality case reviews have not begun, citing lack of an outside facilitator and confidentiality concerns under legal requirements. Southern New Hampshire Doorways declined to facilitate due to liability concerns, and coordination with a gap analysis committee was proposed but no decision was made.
plain_text:
1 | P a g e  
 
City of Nashua 
 Division of Public Health and Community Services 
 
Opioid Fatality Review Committee Workgroup 
 
Wednesday, October 7, 2026 
2:00-3:30 PM 
Facilitator: Bobbie Bagley       Location: Zoom 
Minutes 
 Discussion  
 The committee discussed legal and facilitation barriers to reviewing overdose 
cases. Reviews have not begun because confidentiality is uncertain. It was 
explained why the committee had not progressed to local case reviews: the 
city lacked an outside facilitator, and existing legal requirements created 
confidentiality concerns. The group discussed the limitations of holding the 
reviews as either a community meeting or an official city committee, then 
considered possible facilitator organizations. 
 Case Review Value and Gap Analysis Collaboration. It was described how case 
reviews could reveal service gaps and guide responses for families and people 
who survive overdoses. Coordination with the gap analysis committee was 
proposed, but concerns were also raised about committee’s limited timeline 
and scope; no decision was made. 
 Southern New Hampshire Doorways declined over liability concerns. 
 An outside facilitator could support reviews with city partners contributing 
data. 
Public Comment 
 No public comments
